title: rwb-access queue-write authority: the request and answer element set of the placement admission part of POST /authorise and of the non-human part of GET /me/permissions is named by no source
description: The authority slice of legacy RWB-E2-036 answers one admission for a model or an agent. Three things it must carry are fixed by no source together. (1) The request elements: the caller code, the caller type, the service identity, the target queue, the queue team code, the case, the product group, the reason, the model or agent version and the field IDs. The legacy story names four body fields of the placement (caseId, reason, modelOrAgent, version) and the configuration key of the approved callers list; it names no element of the access call behind the check. (2) The answer elements: admitted, reasonCode, callerType, roleClass, roleCodes, capabilityArea, right, letters, scope, matrixVersion, maskingVersion, productGroup and fieldMarkers. Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operation as POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) and GET /me/permissions and stops there; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A declares neither operation, so it gives no shape. (3) The two values of the caller type (MODEL and AGENT) are the approved callers list's and no list of caller types exists in the reference data this service may read, so the value is carried and recorded, not validated against a list of this service. The story therefore fixes the element names for the realignment and states, in section 11 and 12.1, that the names are this document's until the review with the rwb-integration owner and the service contract owner confirms or renames them. No business value is invented: the matrix version, the letters, the role class, the scope and the product groups stay rows, and the text of MSG-P4-001 is left with the placeholder because no source gives it.
source: Legacy RWB-E2-036 section 12 (PlacementRequest, four body fields, request and response of the monolith endpoint); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md appendix T-A (no API-P4 row for /authorise or /me/permissions) and T3.1 (role, permission, masking_rule); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 14 (IN: POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits, /masking-policies; EVT none); RWB P2 E2036 CON Queue write interface for models and agents - contract v1.md sections 3 and 12.2
section: Story 1, Flow 2 to 12, Data 11, Contract 12.1, Validation and messages 14
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-036 section 12 names PlacementRequest with caseId, reason, modelOrAgent and version and no access-call element; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-001 to API-P4-021 and none of them is /authorise, /me/permissions, /doa-limits or /masking-policies; Arch v5 slide 14 names the two operations and no element; RWB-P2-E2036-CON 12.2 names POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise as consumed and states that the exact JSON element names of the three consumed contracts are not specified by any source
proposed: Keep the element names of section 12.1 as the realignment baseline, carry them in the service contract document of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and reconfirm them with the rwb-integration owner on the consuming side (RWB-P2-E2036-CON 12.2) at the contract review; where a name changes, the change is additive first and the adapter's contract test proves both sides. Keep the caller type as a carried value of the approved callers list and add no list of caller types to rwb_access.

title: rwb-access queue-write authority: the refusal reason code vocabulary and the status each code answers with are fixed by no source
description: The admission refuses for four different reasons that a caller must be able to tell apart: the calling identity has no right to the operation, the subject is not a role of class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, the subject's roles hold no C letter in Queue and allocation, and the admitting role's scope is ALL only. The messages are named by the sources (MSG-P4-002 for a right the role does not include, MSG-P4-001 for no role, MSG-P4-003 for a record outside the scope) but a single message for four causes cannot tell an adapter or an operator which cause it was. No source names a reason code, a code vocabulary, or the status each code answers with; the FSD pairs MSG-P4-002 with 403 for a right and MSG-P4-003 with 404 for a case outside the scope, and a queue is neither a case nor a right of the caller. The story fixes three refusal codes (RIGHT_NOT_HELD, CALLER_KIND and SCOPE_NOT_ALL), keeps the 422 of an empty or out-of-range field on MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-002, keeps the 503 of an unrecorded entry on MSG-P7-003, and records that the vocabulary and the status mapping are this document's until the review.
source: Legacy RWB-E2-036 section 14 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P7-003) and exception paths X10 and X11; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 VR-P4-004-1, AC-ALT-P4-004-02 (403 MSG-P4-002 with the area and the right), AC-EXC-P4-004-01 and VR-P4-011-1 (404 MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope); FSD P4 v3 A2.7 exception flows (AC-DENY entries with a reason)
section: Exception paths 5, Business rules 8 (BR11, BR12), Contract 12.1, Validation and messages 14
evidence: FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-004-1 gives one text for every right refusal and no code; VR-P4-011-1 gives 404 MSG-P4-003 whose text speaks of a case; the legacy story uses MSG-P4-002 for the missing Queue and allocation C right and adds no code; no source in the read list names a reason code or a code vocabulary
proposed: Fix the five reason codes in the service contract document with one status each (403 for RIGHT_NOT_HELD, CALLER_KIND and SCOPE_NOT_ALL; the 422 and 503 codes keep MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-P7-003), keep MSG-P4-002 as the message of every 403, and let the adapter map the code to its own refusal without restating the text.

title: rwb-access queue-write authority: no source binds a role to a list of teams or regions, so a scope narrower than ALL cannot be resolved for a non-human caller
description: The queue targeting of a write is the scope of the caller's role. TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives role exactly one scope value (default_scope, DF-REF-038, LOV-SCOPE OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL) and no table binds a role or a user to a list of team codes or region codes. The legacy story gives a service identity scope All, which needs no list, and the FSD's scope examples are a person whose scope is OWN and a case whose team is MTG-NE, neither of which resolves a team list either. Three consequences follow and the story states them: the queue's team code can only be presented with the request and recorded, never compared; a caller whose admitting role carries a narrower scope is refused with SCOPE_NOT_ALL rather than guessed at; and the profile read answers ALL or the reason it is not, with no queue list. The missing binding table is the gap, and the refusal is the default that keeps the answer safe until a source names the binding.
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T3.1 (role DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039, default_scope DF-REF-038, LOV-SCOPE); FSD P4 v3 A2.1 field catalog (role.default_scope Own, team, region, all) and AC-EXC-P4-004-01 (a case outside the scope); legacy RWB-E2-036 section 12 (Authorization: Queue and allocation, right C; scope All for service identities); Arch v5 slide 41 (P4 owns scope and masking policy; P3 owns queues and queue membership); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (queue, queue_member and assignment are P3's)
section: Flow 6, Exception paths X5, Business rules 8 (BR3), Contract 12.1, Acceptance criteria 7 (AC3, AC4)
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role holds one default_scope value and no binding table appears in T3.1; LOV-SCOPE holds OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL with no list to bind; ownership.json keeps queue and queue_member with P3, so rwb_access cannot enumerate a team list without reading another service's table; the legacy story gives a service identity scope All and therefore never needed the binding
proposed: Admit a non-human caller on scope ALL only, record the presented team code in the access entry and compare it with nothing, and refuse any other scope with SCOPE_NOT_ALL; if a team or region binding is later required for a non-human caller, add it as a versioned row of rwb_access in a matrix version with its own migration and revisit BR3, not as a read of rwb_case.queue.

title: rwb-access queue-write authority: how a caller code is bound to a Workbench role, and whether a caller code is itself a role, is fixed by no source
description: The approved callers list holds a caller code, its type MODEL or AGENT and the service identity it runs under (legacy precondition and BR1; RWB-P2-E2036-CON section 12.2). What the sources do not say is whether the caller code is a role in its own right, whether it narrows the rights of the service identity, or whether it is only a label the entry records. This story resolves the subject through the role of the service identity at the matrix version in force and fails a subject whose role class is not NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, and it records the caller code without resolving it, because (a) the list is the rwb-case parameter and reference-data row read by rwb-integration under DP-06 and DP-07 and rwb-access holds no copy, and (b) TSD P4 T6.1 gives the non-human identities (SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR, SY-AGENT) roles of class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR in one matrix with no per-caller row. If a caller code later has to narrow a right, that is a matrix version change with per-caller rows and a change to this rule.
source: Legacy RWB-E2-036 sections 3 and 8 (BR1: only a caller in the approved callers list, under the service identity listed for it) and section 12 (Authorization); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1 (SY-AGENT and the other non-human identities) and T3.1 (role.role_class, LOV-ROLE-CLASS); RWB P2 E2036 CON 12.2 and 12.8 (the list is consumed from rwb-case and faked); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (parameter_catalog and reference_row are P3's)
section: Story 1, Flow 3, Exception paths X2 and X3, Business rules 8 (BR4), Authority 10, Acceptance criteria 7 (AC5)
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-036 BR1 and precondition name the list with the caller code, the type and the service identity and say nothing about a role per caller; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists the non-human identities as roles with three capability letters and no per-caller row; ownership.json keeps parameter_catalog and reference_row with P3, so the list is not rwb_access data; no source names a caller-to-role column
proposed: Keep the resolution on the service identity's role and the class check NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, record the caller code and the type in the access entry, and hold no copy of the list; if a caller code must narrow a right, raise it as a matrix version change with per-caller rows and re-open BR2 and BR4.

title: rwb-access queue-write authority: the decision code of the access entry for a placement admission and the entry fields beyond the standard record columns are fixed by no source
description: Every admission and every refusal writes one access entry, and the entry is the only audit evidence that a non-human caller wrote to a queue (NFR-078; CTL-06; R-UNI-39). Two parts of it are not fixed. (1) The decision code: FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.8 use AC-READ for a read, AC-EXPT for an export and AC-DENY for a refusal, and the legacy decision record of the placement uses D6, which is also decision code D6 of the route decision in the Drools design; a placement admission is neither a screen read nor an export, so this story uses AC-READ for an admission and AC-DENY for a refusal and records that the choice is its own. (2) The entry fields beyond the standard record columns: the local decision-record library of DP-03 owns the column set and no source gives it, so the story names the values the entry carries (the calling service identity, the caller code, the caller type, the model or agent version, the reason code, the target queue, the team code, the case, the product group, the matrix version, the masking version, the field IDs marked and the time) and leaves the columns to RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.8 (access entries with decision codes AC-READ, AC-EXPT and AC-DENY, the actor, the case and the actions with masked field IDs) and AC-EXC-P4-007-03 (503 MSG-P7-003 and no data); legacy RWB-E2-036 AC3 and BR5 (one decision log entry with decision code D6, the reason, the version and the caller); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (D6 as the route decision code); Arch v5 slide 20 (own schema: outbox, inbox, decision_record); plan DP-03 (local decision-record library)
section: Flow 11, Business rules 8 (BR5), Data 11, Contract 12.3 and 12.7, Validation and messages 14
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.7 gives AC-READ, AC-EXPT and AC-DENY and no placement code; legacy AC3 gives D6 for the placement decision entry, which the Drools design also uses for the route decision D6; Arch v5 slide 20 places decision_record in every service schema and names no column; the ledger entry of the central decision log is P7's and arrives through the library, not through a column list of this service
proposed: Use AC-READ for an admission and AC-DENY for a refusal, keep D6 for the adapter's own admission record where RWB-P2-E2036-CON already uses it, and leave the column set to RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; confirm with Internal audit at the access-log story (RWB-P4-AD007-APP) that a placement admission reads as an access entry and not as a business decision.

title: The roles and letters of the rule-administration area differ between the work package line, the legacy authority table and TSD P4 v3 T6.1, and the legacy access test names a role the matrix gives the right
source: _work/msr/wp/B-P4-12.md story RWB-P4-E2041-APP; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1 and its rule-package refinement, T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.18.3.3; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 041 Rule change governance and audit report v1.md sections 10 and 16
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data; section 16 test case TC-E2-041-11
description: Three sources give the authority of a rule change differently. (1) The work package line of this slice names RW-REFADM and the Compliance role as the roles that may change a rule and speaks of the A letter of the rule-administration capability area; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-COE CRUD with C and U for a rule package, RW-RISK RA with A for the approval, RW-AUDIT, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM and RW-COMPLY R, and RW-REFADM R only, with the explicit note that the reference data administrator prepares the change checklist and the load file with no upload, no approval and no rollback. (2) The legacy story section 10 names RW-COE as the loader, RW-RISK as the approver and RW-AUDIT as the reader, and gives no letter. (3) The legacy access test TC-E2-041-11 makes RW-CASEOWN the role without the Rules and parameters right, while T6.1 gives RW-CASEOWN R in that area. The story reads T6.1 as the source, keeps RW-REFADM as the preparer of the checklist who is answered mayPrepare false, and uses RW-PHONECOL, whose letter is a dash, for the refusal test.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 rows include RW-COE Center of excellence analyst CRUD / CRUD / R; RW-RISK Risk and model risk officer RA / R / dash; RW-AUDIT Internal audit R / R / R; RW-REFADM Reference data administrator R / CRUD / dash; RW-CASEOWN Case owner R / R / dash; RW-PHONECOL Phone collector dash / R / dash. The refinement table of T6.1 reads: RW-REFADM prepares the change checklist and the load file; no upload, no approval and no rollback. Legacy RWB-E2-041 section 10 lists RW-COE with Rules and parameters CRUD and read, RW-RISK with Rules and parameters A, RW-AUDIT with Rules and parameters R. Legacy TC-E2-041-11 reads: RW-CASEOWN, no Rules and parameters right, reads the change report and is refused with MSG-P4-002.
owner_role: Security administrator with the P4 business analyst
proposed: Publish one matrix row set for the RULES_AND_PARAMETERS area that states the letter of every role a rule change touches, restate what the reference data administrator may do without a C letter, and correct TC-E2-041-11 to a role whose letter is a dash so the access test proves the default-denial rule rather than a role that holds R.

title: The record code and the field shape of a rule-change authority and of an audit export inside a decision-record entry are not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.7 and A2.16; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 041 Rule change governance and audit report v1.md sections 8 and 16
section: Section 4 Flow steps 10 and 13; section 8 Business rules BR7; section 11 Data; section 12.3 Events published; section 17 Guardrails
description: FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.16 name three access decision codes - AC-READ for a read, AC-EXPT for an export and AC-DENY for a refusal - and require a list or export read to record the filter, the row count and no case id. The decision-record field set DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 names no capability area, no right, no action, no period, no row count and no version label, and no source gives a record code for a rule-change authority at all. The place these values take inside an entry, and whether a rule-change authority is written under AC-READ or under a code of its own, are therefore a reading and not a source value.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-007-01 requires one entry with decision code AC-READ, the actor, the case id and the field ids; AC-ALT-P4-007-02 requires decision code AC-EXPT, the filter, row count 37 and no case id; AC-EXC-P4-007-04 requires AC-DENY with the area and the right; the LDM entry fields DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 carry no area, right, action, period or count; legacy RWB-E2-041 names no code for a rule change and only the columns of the report.
proposed: Carry the capability area, the right, the action, the version label, the author reference, the period, the package, the format, the row count and the matrix version in the actions list of the decision-record entry, reuse AC-READ, AC-DENY and AC-EXPT rather than minting a fourth code, and add the fields in the next LDM version with audit.

title: The two operations of this slice, and their request and answer shapes, are absent from Architecture v5, the API Specification and the TSD P4 appendix
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14 and 41; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T-A.1 and T6.1; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api section
section: Section 4 Flow steps 2, 9, 11 and 13; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Solution plan
description: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access four inbound REST operations - POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and GET /masking-policies - and slide 41 repeats the same set. TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is an entitlement read for the rule-administration area or an export record; its nearest row, API-P4-020 GET /admin/rule-packages/change-report, is the report itself, which the ownership map places with P7. The two operations this story adds, the action set, the refusal reasons and the answer fields are therefore a design decision the contract review has to confirm, and the story names the fields it needs so that it can be built and tested.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 IN line of rwb-access reads: POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits /masking-policies. TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 has no rule-authority row and no export-record row. ownership.json gives GET /admin/rule-packages/change-report to P7 under ASM-A6-api-3. No source carries the action set PREPARE, APPROVE, READ_REPORT or the refusal reasons NONE, NO_LETTER, PREPARER_IS_APPROVER.
owner_role: Solution architect with the API Specification owner
proposed: Add GET /api/recovery/access/v1/rule-authority and POST /api/recovery/access/v1/rule-report-exports to the API Specification baseline as P4 operations with the query, body and answer fields this story uses, and freeze the action set and the refusal reasons at the contract review of RWB-P3-E2041-CON.

title: Which right a service identity holds to ask this service about a person other than the session user is not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1 and T6.2; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14 and 41 (permission data cached from rwb-access)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 3; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract
description: The four-eyes check is asked about the person who is about to approve, which is usually not the caller: rwb-decision asks about an approver, and the gateway-bff asks about the signed-in user through the same operation. TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists the RW- roles and a few service identities and gives no row to rwb-decision or to the gateway route, and T6.2 says each endpoint declares its capability area and right without naming the rights a service identity holds. The story reads the R letter in RULES_AND_PARAMETERS as the right that lets a caller ask about another person, and cannot say whether a service identity needs a broader right.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 has service rows for SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR and SY-AGENT only; T6.2 describes Entra sign-on, the per-endpoint area and right, and mTLS, with no service-identity rights; Architecture v5 slide 41 P7 IN names REST Access: DoA limits and nothing about a rule authority; no source names the identity of the gateway-bff route inside rwb-access.
proposed: Add the rwb-decision service identity and the gateway-bff route to the permission data with the R letter in RULES_AND_PARAMETERS and nothing else, and confirm it with the security administrator before the authorise contract is frozen.

title: rwb-access rule-package authority: the action vocabulary, the request and answer shape of the rule-package part of POST /authorise and the access-log decision code of a rule-package change are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-access IN: POST /authorise with role, scope and DoA) and slide 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1, T6.3, API-P4-017 to API-P4-019 and T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4, A2.7 and A2.8; Legacy RWB-E2-042 sections 7, 10 and 12
section: Section 1 Story; section 4 Flow steps 1 to 3 and 11; section 5 Exception paths X1, X2; section 7 AC7; section 11 Data; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Components and Build steps
description: Three values this slice needs are absent. (1) Architecture v5 slide 14 names POST /authorise with role, scope and DoA only, and no source gives a rule-package action, so the five action names (LOAD, APPROVE, ROLLBACK, DRY_RUN, EVALUATE), the request fields (action, packageCode, versionLabel, authorRef, capabilityArea, right, caseRef) and the answer fields (authorised, reason, matrixVersion, area, right, packageArea, entryRef) are a read rather than a source value. (2) FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.8 name only three access-log decision codes (AC-READ, AC-EXPT, AC-DENY), so no code exists for a privileged rule-package change; this story uses AC-CHG for a load, an approval and a rollback and leaves AC-READ and AC-DENY as the source names them. (3) The right each action needs is fixed from TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and API-P4-017 to API-P4-019 (C for a load, A for an approval, U for a rollback, R for a dry run), but no source states the rule as data, so the mapping is carried as the contract of section 12.1 with a contract test rather than as a row of a table this service owns.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 reads 'rwb-access (P4, Access & administration) IN: REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits | /masking-policies' with no rule-package element; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-014 to API-P4-020 for the rule packages and none of them is the authorise path; FSD P4 v3 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 writes decision code 'AC-READ', AC-ALT-P4-007-02 writes 'AC-EXPT' and AC-EXC-P4-007-04 writes 'AC-DENY', and no code for a change appears anywhere in A2.7 or A2.8.
area: rwb-access authorise contract and access log
proposed: Add the rule-package action, its request and answer fields and a change decision code to the authorise contract when RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published, agree the code with the access-log owner of the legacy RWB-E1-039 slice, and stub both in the contract fake.

title: rwb-access rule-package authority: the scope of a running service identity inside rwb-access and the capability area each rule package serves are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (service identities and the P4 DB line); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 (SY-RULES R) and T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 (evaluation local in the owning service); Legacy RWB-E2-042 sections 10 and 19
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC6; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Two values are missing. (1) Architecture v5 gives every service a service identity for jobs and agents (TSD P4 v3 T6.2, NFR-051) and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives SY-RULES the R letter in Rules and parameters, but no source states which identity reads a model, what a service identity may do in the other thirteen capability areas, or whether the rwb-decision identity that calls the authorise path holds a user-equivalent role. (2) The capability area a package decides in is not stated: RESTRUCTURE serves Treatment and offer, and no source names the area of PAYMENT_MATCH or BOOKING_MATCH, so this story takes the area from rwb-decision as packageArea and tests only RESTRUCTURE with TREATMENT_AND_OFFER.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives P4 'Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log' with no service-identity row; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists 'SY-RULES Drools evaluator | R | R | -' under the three columns Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only, and T6.2 says 'service identities for jobs and agents' with no scope; Temporal and Drools Design slide 15 says 'evaluation is local in the one service that owns each model' with no area; Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 10 names SY-RULES as 'Drools evaluator' and gives it no scope.
proposed: Publish the service-identity rows of the permission matrix with the fourteen areas, confirm with the platform identity owner that each service runs as one non-human actor, and record the area each package serves as a package attribute of rwb-decision.

title: rwb-access rule-package authority: TSD P4 v3 gives P4 the four rule tables, while Architecture v5 and the ownership ruling put the rule registry in P7
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 and T6.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case owned by P7, ASM-A6-tables-3); Legacy RWB-E2-042 sections 11 and 12
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 8 BR8; section 11 Data; section 12.7 Tables owned; section 19 Out of scope
description: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 declares that P4 owns rule_package (DF-REF-274 to 278), rule_package_version (279 to 295), rule_row (001 to 015 and 052 to 054, with 296 to 298 added) and rule_test_case (185 to 197, with 299 added), and T6.1 gives P4 the upload, approve, dry-run and rollback rights over them. Architecture v5 slides 27 and 41 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 15 keep authoring, four-eyes approval, effective dating and version audit central in rwb-decision, and the R-PREC default ruling with ASM-A6-tables-3 puts the four tables in P7. The higher-precedence sources win, so this slice holds no rule table and answers only the authority, and the loser is recorded here.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 reads 'P4 owns the four rule tables: rule_package (DF-REF-274 to 278), rule_package_version (279 to 295), rule_row ... and rule_test_case ...'; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P7 'approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry' and slide 27 reads 'Governance stays central in rwb-decision: authoring, test scenarios, four-eyes approval, effective dating, audit of every version'; ownership.json gives the four tables owner P7 with ruling 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision ... despite TSD P4 v3 and TSD P3 v3 declaring these tables'.
proposed: Correct TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T6.1 in the next version so that the four rule tables and the registry operations are P7's, and keep the P4 rows for the rights and the access log only.

title: rwb-access rule-package authority: the lifetime of a cached authorise answer, the refresh trigger of the cached permission data and the granularity of the access-log entry of a dry run are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 ('Access: authorise (cached)'), slide 11 (2 s timeout, circuit breaker, GET retry once) and slide 20; DP-11; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 19
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 13; section 7 AC5; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.4 Events consumed; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Architecture v5 names the authorise decision 'cached' and DP-11 fixes one hop with a 2 s timeout, but no source gives the lifetime of a cached answer, the size of the cache, or whether a refused answer is cached with an allowed one. The event that refreshes a cached answer is likewise unnamed: this story drops it on rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 keyed by the matrix version, which is this service's own event and is raised by the permission-matrix slice. The dry run reads the registry's counts over 412 open cases in AC5, and no source says whether one entry covers the dry run or one entry is written per case.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 OUT line of rwb-access reads 'REST Access: authorise (cached)' with no lifetime and slide 11 gives the 2 s timeout and the retry only; TSD P4 v3 T6.2 describes the access check and names no cache; FSD P4 v3 A2.7 tests a read and a refusal and no expiry; Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 19 lists the load, scenario, approval and rollback mechanics as out of scope and says nothing about caching.
area: rwb-access decision cache and access-log granularity
proposed: Fix the lifetime as a parameter row of the parameters contract (DP-06) at the wave 2 design review, keep the version-keyed drop so the tests do not depend on the clock, and confirm with the access-log owner that one entry covers one dry run.

title: No DoA-specific load, approve, rollback or version-read operation is specified for rwb-access
description: The legacy story names only the generic reference-load operations of the monolith, and the Ownership Map assigns those paths (the load, its approve, its verify and its rollback) to P3 rwb-case under ASM-A6-api-4. delegation_limit is P4's table and P4 is its only writer, so this slice needs its own admin operations under /api/recovery/access/v1, and no source names them or their request and response field sets. The shape of the difference report that RW-RISK reviews before approving is also not specified.
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 038, sections 4, 12 and 13; Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3, appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-005, API-P4-006, API-P4-010); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api ruling on the reference-load paths (ASM-A6-api-4)
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 lists API-P4-005, API-P4-006, API-P4-009 and API-P4-010 on the generic reference-load paths of the monolith; ownership.json gives those paths to P3 with the ruling that parameters and reference data are P3's; no source names a delegation_limit load path in rwb_access and no source gives the difference report a shape
proposed: Four operations of rwb-access under /api/recovery/access/v1: POST /admin/doa-loads, POST /admin/doa-loads/{loadId}/approve, POST /admin/doa-loads/{loadId}/rollback and GET /admin/doa-versions, with the DoaLoad, DoaVersion, DifferenceReport and RollbackRequest shapes of section 12.1

title: The rollback of a delegation version has no acceptance criterion, business rule or window semantics
description: TSD P4 v3 API-P4-010 and FSD P4 v3 A2.22 (FEAT-ADM-06) name a one-call rollback of a reference data version, and RWB-P4-E2013-APP's preconditions place the DoA rollback in this story, but the legacy story has no rollback route, no rule on what happens to valid_from and valid_to of the two versions, no statement of who may roll it back and no acceptance criterion that tests it.
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3, appendix T-A.2 API-P4-010; Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3, A2.22; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 038, sections 1 to 13; Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1, RWB P4 E2013 APP, section 3
evidence: The legacy story moves a version from Loaded to Approved and closes the previous version, and says nothing about reopening it; API-P4-010 calls a rollback and names its rights only; no criterion of RWB-E1-038 covers a rollback
proposed: Rollback is one call by the parameter's approver role with Reference data U and the same four-eyes rule, reverses the window of the rolled-back version and of the version before it, refuses a version whose window has closed, writes one AC-VERS entry with change kind rolled back and publishes DoaLimitChanged; a test case is added to the test set at the next story revision

title: The payload, key and publication point of rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 are not specified
description: Architecture v5 names the event and its topic in the rwb-access contract and in the event catalogue, and says only that the consumers refresh a cache. No source gives the event a payload, a key, a change kind or a CloudEvents version, and none says whether it is published on the load, on the approval or on both.
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slide 14 (rwb-access OUT), slide 20 and the event catalogue row for AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives the topic rwb.access.events.v1 and the event names AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged; the event catalogue row gives the producer and the consumers only; no payload or key is written anywhere
proposed: CloudEvents 1.0 on rwb.access.events.v1, key limitVersion, payload limitVersion, table, change kind (loaded, approved, rolled back), validFrom, validTo and rowCount, no personal data, published by the outbox relay after the transaction commits

title: Publishing DoaLimitChanged needs the outbox library of DP-09, which this slice's dependency list and pattern list do not carry
description: The event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the version state, and the outbox and inbox library of DP-09 is a platform contract story (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON). The slice's build dependency list carries eight H rows and none is the outbox library, and DP-09 is not in the slice's pattern list, so the dependency that makes the publication possible is not recorded where a build team looks for it.
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, section R5.5 table row DP-09 and the slice dependency list in _work/msr/wp/B-P4-12.md; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slide 11 (transactional outbox) and slide 20 (outbox and inbox in every service schema)
section: 12.3 Events published; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan
evidence: The pattern list of RWB-P4-E1038-APP is DP01, DP03, DP04, DP06, DP07, DP08, DP11, DP13, DP15 and DP19; DP-09 would add H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, and the slice has no such H row although it publishes an event
proposed: The outbox, inbox and idempotency tables exist in rwb_access as library objects created by the P4 ACE DB story, the outbox relay JOB-11 publishes, and the dependency on the library contract sits with the service baseline rather than with this story; the metadata row is left as the WP fixes it and the dependency is added at service-baseline review

title: FSD P4 v3 gives the DoA feature to the Security administrator as primary actor, while the story, the parameter and the criteria give RW-REFADM as loader and RW-RISK as approver
description: FSD P4 v3 A2.6.3.3 names the Security administrator (RW-SECADM) as primary actor of FEAT-ACA-06 and the product heads and Risk as also-users, and its A2.6.2 description says the actor opens a screen and enters values. The legacy story, the legacy criteria AC1 and AC5 and the parameter rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit=RW-RISK say RW-REFADM loads and RW-RISK approves, and no screen exists in wave 1. The two statements cannot both hold.
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3, A2.6.2, A2.6.3.3 and A2.6.4; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 038, sections 3, 4, 7 and 10
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6.3.3 role table: Security administrator primary, product head and Risk and model risk officer also uses; AC1 and AC5 of RWB-E1-038: U-3101 holds RW-REFADM and loads, U-3102 holds RW-RISK and approves, U-3103 holding RW-PRODHEAD is refused
proposed: The story, its criteria and the approver-role parameter win: RW-REFADM holds Reference data C and loads, and the parameter's role approves and rolls back; the FSD A2.6 role table is read as the generic feature-role table and is corrected at the next FSD revision

title: Which story owns the DDL of the five rwb_access authority tables is stated twice
description: This WP assigns the rwb_access share of RWB-E1-001 to RWB-P4-E1001-APP: the role, permission, role_conflict, masking_rule and delegation_limit tables with their keys, constraints, indexes, dictionary rows and the Flyway baseline for rwb_access under DP-15. The sibling stories of the same service already state that RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E1037-CON delivered the rwb_access baseline with those five tables and their dictionary rows. Two stories therefore create the same five tables unless one reading wins, and a double CREATE TABLE fails the pipeline.
source: WP B-P4-12 (RWB-P4-E1001-APP slice) against the preconditions of RWB-P4-E1007-APP, RWB-P4-E1008-APP, RWB-P4-E1018-APP, RWB-P4-E1019-APP, RWB-P4-E2002-APP, RWB-P4-E2004-APP and RWB-P4-E2007-APP
owner_role: Solution architect with the TechX tech lead
evidence: The WP names the five tables, their keys, constraints, indexes, dictionary rows and the Flyway baseline as this story's deliverable; the sibling stories' preconditions say RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E1037-CON 'delivered the rwb_access baseline: the tables role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit, their dictionary rows'
proposed: Confirm that the DDL, the keys, the indexes and the migration of the five tables are RWB-P4-E1001-APP's, and read every sibling reference to the 'rwb_access baseline' as 'the version this story applies'. RWB-P4-E1037-CON keeps the contract stub and creates no table.

title: The exact per-service table list of rwb_access is not stated in one place
description: No source lists which of the 92 tables land in rwb_access. The Ownership Map gives P4 exactly five tables (role, permission, role_conflict, masking_rule, delegation_limit), while TSD P4 v3 T3.1 also defines lov_value, partner_user and the four rule tables, which the ownership rulings move to P3 (lov_value), S9 (partner_user) and P7 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case). The per-service table list has to be fixed before the migration is written, because a table created in the wrong schema is a cross-schema read waiting to happen.
source: Ownership Map (ownership.json) against TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 and Architecture v5 slide 41
evidence: ownership.json gives role, permission, role_conflict, masking_rule and delegation_limit the owner P4 with no ruling of their own, and gives lov_value P3, partner_user S9 and the four rule tables P7 with explicit rulings; TSD P4 v3 declares all nine tables in the P4 module
proposed: Fix rwb_access at exactly the five authority tables and treat the TSD P4 v3 declarations of lov_value, partner_user and the rule tables as the monolith's module view, superseded by the ownership rulings and Architecture v5 slide 41.

title: The dictionary rows of the five rwb_access tables have no seeding owner after the split
description: The 44 business fields of the five tables carry Field IDs in TSD P4 v3 T3.1, but the dictionary itself is one dictionary in rwb_source_data under the P1 ruling, so a per-service dictionary write would be a cross-schema write. The Field IDs of the 7 standard columns on each of the five tables are also not given, so the 35 standard-column rows cannot be cited. No source says which mechanism carries a service's own field rows into the one dictionary.
source: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.0; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; legacy RWB-E1-001 sections 11 and 13; RWB-P1-E1001-APP
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026, DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-044, DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062 and DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-211 but no Field ID for is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at or updated_by; the legacy story seeded all 1,366 rows from one migration in one schema
proposed: Declare the 44 business rows as a build artefact of this story, hand the declaration to the one dictionary's seed in rwb_source_data, and let the seed carry the 35 standard-column rows under its own Field IDs. Cite the 44 business Field IDs only.

title: The file name and sequence number of the rwb_access baseline migration are not fixed
description: The naming rule of D-RCV-28 fixes the shape V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql with a four-digit sequence taken in merge order, but no source gives the sequence number this story takes on the rwb-access pipeline, and the legacy baseline holds version 1.001 of schema recovery. The version this story applies has to be later than every service-baseline version and must not reuse the legacy 1.001 line.
source: Legacy RWB-E1-001 sections 12 and 13; D-RCV-28 naming rule; WP B-P4-12
evidence: The legacy file is V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql with a four-digit sequence 0001 in schema recovery; the per-service sequence of rwb-access and its next free number are not in any source read for this WP
proposed: Write the file as V<seq>__rwb_p4_e1001_access_schema.sql, take the four-digit sequence at merge in the rwb-access pipeline, and assert in the test that it is later than every service-baseline version and never 0001 of the legacy line.

title: The constraint names and the full index set of the five tables are not specified
description: TSD P4 v3 T3.3 gives only the relationships (permission to role, and none for the other four tables), and no source gives the names of the primary keys, unique keys, check constraints or indexes of the five tables, nor the column order of the indexes the read paths need. The physical schema of the monolith names its own constraints, but those names are the legacy marker and not the target.
source: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.3; Physical Schema v6; WP B-P4-12
owner_role: ACE team (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
evidence: T3.3 lists five relationships across the module and nothing about the keys of role, role_conflict, masking_rule or delegation_limit; the read paths of RWB-P4-E2013-APP, RWB-P4-E1019-APP and the masking answer of RWB-P4-E2016 name the predicates but not an index
proposed: Take the platform naming convention for the constraint names, keep the primary key on id, make role_code unique, keep the single foreign key permission.role_id, and create one index per read path with the leading columns of section 13; the plan check of AC10 guards the result.

title: role.entra_group is a column in the technical specification and not a Workbench column in the functional one
description: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives role.entra_group Field ID DF-REF-039, varchar(120), sourced from Entra ID. FSD P4 v3, re-based on the ACE database, states that the Entra group is read from v_ace_iam_group and is not a Workbench column. A column created on one reading is a copy of an ACE fact on the other, which the boundary rule forbids.
source: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-039) against FSD P4 v3 change note and field catalog
evidence: The TSD field table lists entra_group under role with DF-REF-039 and source 'Entra ID'; the FSD field catalog says 'v_ace_iam_group.entra_group ... read from ACE (iam_group, RWB-ACE-001); not a Workbench column'
proposed: Keep the column because the technical specification outranks the functional one in R-PREC, create it nullable and empty, and read the mapping at run time through the rwb-source-data contract so no ACE fact is copied or maintained here.
